prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. Asset: paired production backgrounds for a Mars making game. Create ONE high-resolution near-square diptych canvas, exactly two equally wide edge-to-edge TALL portrait paintings side by side, LEFT and RIGHT, each about 390:844 aspect, straight vertical division at 50%, no border, gutter, labels or text. Each painting must be a complete independent game background with narrative scenery confined to its upper 38 percent and broad QUIET empty ochre ground in its lower 62 percent. View looking slightly downward across a working apron. Input 1 is the established Mars scene STYLE and terrain reference. Input 2 is equipment MATERIAL/STYLE reference only, do not copy its poster or text. Restrained tangible retro-industrial realism, warm cream painted metal, teal hardware, exposed steel, charcoal seals, fine restrained handling wear and dust, natural Martian sunlight, matching detailed painterly physical rendering. No people, UI, words or decorative framing.
Both panels show EXACTLY THE SAME landed spacecraft and starter habitat from the same camera. On left at 27% width, 24% height within each panel is the rounded cream habitat pressure wall; on right at 70% width, 25% height is the grounded lower support of a small staged lander. Lander upper cabin occupies upper-right: squat cream octagonal capsule, two dark front windows, teal circular hatch collar, short ladder, exposed steel lower landing frame. The upper cabin/tanks are intact. A lower leg on the near side has folded sideways, tilting the cabin slightly; ladder stops short of ground. Low red basalt hill and small cave opening behind, far mesas consistent. Ground-level emergency rack at habitat edge. Keep both interactive features wholly inside the central 82% width of their individual panels. No solar arrays, furnace, farm, fuel plant or other future construction.
LEFT panel: opening accident. Habitat has a small jagged stone puncture in its visible cream wall at 27%,24%, distinct dark hole and a lodged reddish stone; lower lander frame settles onto loose shifted rubble at 70%,25%. NO patch or temporary support yet. Empty ground below.
RIGHT panel: return for permanent repair later. Habitat now bears a conspicuous small square clamped cream-and-teal pressure patch over exactly that hole. Same lander remains tilted, same folded original leg, but its low side is safely carried on a squat stacked STEEL CRIB of short cross-braced lengths and broad plates. The original wrecked strut remains visible beside it. Ground immediately left of that crib is loose and unprepared. No new permanent leg or level cabin yet. Empty ground below.
The comparison should show that shelter is repaired and the original damaged lander was stabilized, while a permanent leg still remains to be built. Make physical causes visually legible at phone scale; do not use diagrams or arrows.
Feasibility constraint: ALL locally made structures use a lone astronaut's basic drill/driver, cutter, spanners and forming tools. The temporary crib is simple cut stock steel with ordinary bolted overlaps and broad plates, modest imperfect joints; no welded sculpture, custom cast or milled fittings, ornate trusswork or precision shop-made hardware. Cream factory finish belongs only to imported cabin/habitat.
